data.name: Vasudev
data.gender_notes: Vasudev is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Vasudev means ‘all-pervading God.’ It is a compound name derived from two Sanskrit words: ‘vasu’ meaning ‘dwelling’ and ‘dev’ meaning ‘God.’ Thus, Vasudev can be translated as ‘the God who pervades all.’ This name is associated with Lord Vishnu, who is believed to be the preserver of the universe in Hinduism. The name Vasudev carries the meaning “All-Pervading God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Vasudev usually hope their child will grow to embody all-pervading god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Vasudev is considered sacred in Hinduism. It is believed that invoking the name of Vasudev brings peace, prosperity, and protection to one’s life. It is also believed that the name Vasudev has the power to ward off negative energies and bring positivity.
data.etymology: Vasudev belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “All-Pervading God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vasudev total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Vasudev holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism, as it is associated with Lord Vishnu, one of the primary deities in the Hindu pantheon. The name is often used in religious texts, hymns, and sacred chants to invoke the divine presence of Lord Vishnu. In Mahabharata, one of the two major Sanskrit epics of Ancient India, the character Bhishma was addressed as Vasudeva Anudasanna, meaning one who acknowledges the supremacy of Lord Vishnu. Moreover, Vasudev is also a common name for Hindu deities believed to represent Lord Vishnu in various incarnations and manifestations.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Vasudev signifies the divine presence that resides within and pervades all things in the universe. It is a reminder that our essence is not limited to our physical bodies, but rather is a part of the divine consciousness that connects us to the cosmos. The name also carries the significant spiritual message of universal love and compassion. Lord Vishnu, as Vasudev, is the protector of the universe and represents the divine love and compassion that nurtures and sustains all life. Therefore, the name Vasudev can serve as a powerful reminder of the interconnectedness of all beings and the divine love that binds us together.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vasudev symbolizes universal consciousness and love. His name, derived from Vasu meaning 'dwellers' and Dev meaning 'God', signifies one who embodies the presence of all gods within himself. It's a reminder that the divine resides within us all.

historical_references.reference: Vasudev is mentioned in the Mahabharata as the father of Lord Krishna. He is also called 'Devakiputra' or 'Devaki's son'. Vasudev is described as a king of the Yadavas, a branch of the lunar dynasty of ancient India.

historical_references.reference: The Puranas describe Vasudev as an avatar or manifestation of Lord Vishnu. He is also known as 'Vasudeva-Krishna' or 'Vasudeva-Hari'. The story goes that when the demon king Kamsa was threatening to destroy the Yadavas, Vasudev and his wife, Devaki, hid their newborn son Krishna from him by exchanging him with another newborn boy named Govardhana.

In Hindu mythology, Vasudev is identified with Vishnu, and is known as the universal father. In the modern context, the name Vasudev is seen on various platforms. In Hindu rituals, Vasudev is invoked during the 'Shanti Path' (peace path) ceremony, as a symbol of peace and prosperity. In Television, the name Vasudev is used in various shows such as 'Mahabharat' and 'Ramayan,' where characters with this name have significant roles. In the film industry, famous actors like Vasudev Shastri and Vasudev S. Sajjan have made a mark with their performances. In religious texts like the Bhagavad Gita and the Mahabharata, Vasudev is mentioned as a significant character and is revered for his divine qualities. The name continues to hold cultural relevance and is a source of inspiration for many Hindus.
